title: Tiered dialogue qcache and quantization recommendations - draft
content:
Executive summary:

This memo captures a set of pragmatic recommendation presets and a lightweight rollout plan for conversational (dialogue-style) workloads with mixed interaction patterns. The focus is on: 1) tiered qcache TTLs and prefetch rules for short vs session-long dialogs; 2) quantization profile per workload cohort (fast-turn vs long-form); and 3) batching presets that respect latency SLOs while improving GPU utilization. The attached simulation workbook (linked_artifacts) was used to validate the recommendations across three synthetic cohorts.

Why this is different:
- Most prior docs optimize for either session-heavy or throughput-heavy extremes. This draft proposes a 3-tier approach (ephemeral, conversational, archived) to capture real product usage diversity and show deterministic cost/latency tradeoffs.

Assumptions used in simulations:
- Average token lengths and reply lengths per cohort recorded in the spreadsheet tab "cohorts".
- Model baseline: open-7B-v2 CPU/GPU profile used in cost sims with standard KV cache hit cost assumptions.
- Baseline tail-latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for interactive tiers.
- Expected cold-start warming behavior: first request 1.0x token cost, subsequent hits reduce marginal cost per token.

Recommended presets (defaults to expose in Optimize presets UI):
1) Ephemeral (short interactions, one-off queries)
   - qcache TTL: 30s
   - qcache max-prefix-length: 16 tokens
   - batch_size target: 4 (adaptive up to 8 only if latency < 120ms)
   - quantization: int8-ptq on weight-only, dynamic activations
   - expected cost impact vs baseline: ~18-23% reduction
   - rationale: small TTL avoids stale cache pollution while still capturing immediate repeated reasks.

2) Conversational (multi-turn, active sessions)
   - qcache TTL: 45m per-session entry; session-level TTL eviction on inactivity
   - qcache strategy: prefix-sensitive (cache common opening prompts separately)
   - qcache prefetch: warm next-turn KV on response completion for known-turn patterns (stochastic prefetch with p=0.6)
   - batch_size target: 8 (scales to 16 under >80% CPU/GPU idle for throughput windows)
   - quantization: mixed-int8 for MLPs + 4-bit QAT candidate for attention kernels (experimental)
   - expected cost impact: 30-45% reduction depending on session reuse
   - rationale: longer TTLs capture multi-turn reuse; stochastic prefetch smooths tail spikes while limiting wasted work.

3) Archived/low-frequency (rare lookups, long-lived context)
   - qcache TTL: 24h but archive-marked storage with cold-path on first access
   - qcache max-prefix-length: 256 tokens (support long-context retrievals)
   - batch_size target: no aggressive batching; prioritize single-request latency (target p95 <= 500ms)
   - quantization: 4-bit post-training + activation clipping heuristics (cost-focused, lower fidelity acceptable)
   - expected cost impact: 40-60% reduction vs baseline for archival accesses where quality tolerance is higher

Operational knobs and fallbacks:
- Automatic fallback to less-quantized variant when eval monitors detect >3% regression on quality testcases for any cohort in a rolling 1h window.
- Canary rollout path: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% using per-cohort metrics; revert if quality or p95 latency regressions exceed thresholds.
- Adaptive autoscaling: use model of per-shard qcache hit rate to reduce hot-shard replicas during sustained high hit rates.

Cost model notes and sensitivity:
- The spreadsheet runs a sweep over qcache hit rate (10-90%), batch latency vs throughput curves, and quant accuracy penalty. Results show strongest wins when session reuse > 30% and batchable traffic >= 35%.
- Example: For a medium customer (200rps, avg reply 60 tokens), applying conversational presets yields ~38% lower per-token spend and improves throughput by ~2.1x during peak windows. See spreadsheet tab "sim-results".

Implementation checklist (engineering):
- Add three preset entries to Optimize UI with names: Ephemeral, Conversational, Archived (product-optimize/UX ticket).
- Implement stochastic prefetch hook with probability tunable via feature flag (SRE: feature-flag + observability metrics).
- Add quantized fallback variant selection in runtime (serving-runtime PR with model variant tagging).
- Spreadsheet-driven autotune job: iterate qcache TTL and prefetch p for each customer cohort in a nightly job (pipeline spec in linked JIRA).

Testing plan and metrics to surface:
- Primary metrics: per-request cost, p50/p95 latency, qcache hit rate, quality regression delta on golden prompt set, batch utilization.
- Short A/B: run presets vs baseline on 2 pilot customers for 14 days and capture cost delta and any user-facing regressions.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- QAT vs PTQ: whether to push experimental 4-bit QAT into production for conversational tier — requires extra eval gating and retrain cycles.
- Prefetch conservatism: initial p=0.4 vs p=0.6 tradeoffs need live A/B to measure wasted work vs latency smoothing.
- Long-prefix cache memory footprint: archival tier prefix length increases per-shard memory pressure; need SRE input on shard sizing.

Next steps (owner: Aisha Kumar):
- Finalize preset names and default values with product and SRE by 2026-02-14.
- Schedule a short pilot with two customers (one session-heavy, one ephemeral-heavy) for March 2026.
- Create PR template for runtime changes and link to JIRA-OPT-772.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive to produce clear A/B candidates and spreadsheet simulations. Please call out any obviously optimistic assumptions around quantization quality. Also, if you have links to real customer telemetry that match these cohorts, paste them into the spreadsheet and ping me.

— Aisha
